ei.title: Getbol: A Treasure House with Great Potential
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Getbol, a Symbol of Biodiversity Have you ever visited the Korean tidal flats known as getbol? Getbol is a muddy and flat environment that is exposed at low tide and is covered by water at high tide. Soil on land has flowed into the sea and accumulated for more than 8,500 years, creating one of the thickest tidal layers in the world. Since the soil includes organic matter from land animals and plants, getbol is rich in nutrients and provides habitats for thousands of species. In fact, getbol is home to approximately 2,150 species of plants and animals, including 22 globally threatened or near-threatened species. Thanks to its rich biodiversity, getbol is visited by about 118 species of migratory birds every year. For millions of migratory birds that travel between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover location. Without getbol, they would not have a place to rest and feed themselves during their long journeys, and they would become extinct. Since getbol is not only a unique ecosystem crowded with diverse species but also a resting place for endangered birds, it was added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021. The list includes the four tidal flats on the western and southern coasts of Korea: Seocheon Getbol, Gochang Getbol, Shinan Getbol, and Boseong-Suncheon Getbol. Climate Change and Carbon When people think of a changing climate, images of melting glaciers and polar bears losing their habitat often come to mind. But this is only one aspect of the problem. Climate change is causing extreme weather conditions, which have become more frequent and intense worldwide. Heatwaves, droughts, floods, and wildfires are affecting countries around the world. In the autumn of 2019, for example, Australia was hit by one of the worst wildfires on record. Over six months, the wildfires burned about 10 million hectares of land, and killed hundreds of millions of animals. Approximately 30 percent of the koalas in the region are said to have been killed due to the fires. This is why the international community has been seeking solutions to the climate crisis. In 2015, 195 countries signed the Paris Agreement to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. The countries agreed upon the fact that the increase in atmospheric carbon is a major reason for climate change. One key strategy to combat it is to achieve “carbon neutrality,” which involves maintaining a balance between the amount of carbon emitted and carbon absorbed. The Earth’s Atmosphere Is Like a Bathtub Let’s imagine that the Earth’s atmosphere is a large bathtub, and the greenhouse gases emitted into the atmosphere are like water flowing from a tap into the bathtub. At the bottom of the bathtub, there’s a drain that lets the water out. If we keep the tap running, the water level in the bathtub will rise, just as greenhouse gas emissions have led to an increase in atmospheric carbon. This rise in carbon levels has already resulted in negative environmental consequences, such as climate change. To make matters worse, if the water is not effectively drained, the bathtub will overflow. In other words, if we don't reduce carbon emissions sufficiently, atmospheric carbon will continue to accumulate. Blue Carbon and Getbol One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon in the atmosphere is to use the “good” carbon on Earth. The Earth’s carbon can be divided into three types: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon. Black carbon is released while burning fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, and gas. It causes the greenhouse effect, leading to global warming and climate change. Green carbon, on the other hand, is carbon absorbed by and stored in land ecosystems, such as rainforests like the Amazon in South America. It plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem because it absorbs carbon dioxide through photosynthesis. Finally, blue carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangrove wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes. The carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems is about 50 times faster than that of land ecosystems. Blue carbon can store up to 10 times more carbon per unit area than forests on land, making it highly cost-effective. A notable example of blue carbon can be found in tidal flats located around the ocean. Research conducted in 2021 has revealed that getbol in Korea stores approximately 13 million tons of carbon and absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year. This means that getbol alone can offset the carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars in a year. Considering that getbol contains numerous organisms and marine animals that store carbon, the treasure house of blue carbon has become a promising and sustainable solution to the current environmental problem. Scientists worldwide are continuing to explore the capabilities of tidal flats with the goal of having them officially recognized as blue carbon. Efforts to Protect Getbol Getbol in Korea was once considered useless muddy land, so much of it has been reclaimed for farming and urbanization. This has led to a decline in the area of tidal flats, causing a loss of biodiversity. To prevent further damage to the marine ecosystem, both the government and environmental organizations have been making efforts to protect the tidal flats by regulating unnecessary development. Without further efforts to restore getbol, we would fail to preserve this valuable ecosystem for future generations.

questions.passage: Getbol is a muddy and flat environment that is (A)[exposed / hidden] at low tide and is covered by water at high tide. Soil on land has flowed into the sea and accumulated for more than 8,500 years, creating one of the (B)[thickest / thinnest] tidal layers in the world. Since the soil includes (C)[organic / artificial] matter from land animals and plants, getbol is rich in nutrients and provides habitats for thousands of species. In fact, getbol is home to approximately 2,150 species of plants and animals, including 22 globally threatened or near-threatened species.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① exposed(드러난)+thickest(가장 두꺼운)+organic(유기의): 갯벌은 썰물 때 '드러나고', 세계에서 '가장 두꺼운' 갯벌층 중 하나이며, 흙이 육지 동식물의 '유기' 물질을 포함한다는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ② hidden(숨겨진)은 '썰물 때 드러난다(exposed at low tide)'는 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ thinnest(가장 얇은)는 '세계에서 가장 두꺼운 갯벌층'이라는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ artificial(인공의)은 육지 동식물에서 나온 '유기(organic)' 물질이라는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: exposed=드러난, thickest=가장 두꺼운, organic=유기의

questions.passage: But this is only one aspect of the problem. Climate change is causing (A)[extreme / mild] weather conditions, which have become more frequent and intense worldwide. Heatwaves, droughts, floods, and wildfires are affecting countries around the world. In the autumn of 2019, for example, Australia was hit by one of the (B)[worst / mildest] wildfires on record. Over six months, the wildfires (C)[burned / cooled] about 10 million hectares of land, and killed hundreds of millions of animals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① mild(온화한)은 더 잦고 강해진 '극심한(extreme)' 기상 조건이라는 문맥과 반대
✅ ② extreme(극심한)+worst(최악의)+burned(태웠다): 극심한 기상, 기록상 '최악의' 산불, 약 1,000만 헥타르의 땅을 '태웠다'는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ③ mildest(가장 온화한)는 '기록상 최악의 산불'이라는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ cooled(식혔다)는 땅을 '태웠다(burned)'는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: extreme=극심한, worst=최악의, burned=태웠다

questions.passage: Finally, blue carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangrove wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes. The carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems is about 50 times (A)[faster / slower] than that of land ecosystems. Blue carbon can store up to 10 times more carbon per unit area than forests on land, making it highly (B)[cost-effective / costly]. A notable example of blue carbon can be found in tidal flats located around the ocean. Research conducted in 2021 has revealed that getbol in Korea stores approximately 13 million tons of carbon and absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year. This means that getbol alone can (C)[offset / increase] the carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars in a year.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① slower(더 느린)는 해양 생태계의 탄소 흡수율이 육상보다 '약 50배 더 빠르다(faster)'는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② costly(비용이 많이 드는)는 단위 면적당 10배 더 많이 저장해 '비용 효율이 높다(cost-effective)'는 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ increase(늘리다)는 갯벌이 자동차 11만 대의 배출량을 '상쇄한다(offset)'는 문맥과 반대
✅ ④ faster(더 빠른)+cost-effective(비용 효율이 높은)+offset(상쇄하다): 흡수율이 50배 빠르고, 비용 효율이 높으며, 배출량을 상쇄한다는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
det.tip: faster=더 빠른, cost-effective=비용 효율이 높은, offset=상쇄하다

questions.passage: Getbol is a ①<u>muddy</u> and flat environment that is exposed at low tide and is covered by water at high tide.  Soil on land has flowed into the sea and ②<u>accumulated</u> for more than 8,500 years, creating one of the thickest tidal layers in the world.  Since the soil includes organic matter from land animals and plants, getbol is rich in nutrients and ③<u>blocks</u> habitats for thousands of species.  In fact, getbol is home to approximately 2,150 species of plants and animals, including 22 ④<u>globally</u> threatened or near-threatened species.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ blocks → provides: 갯벌은 수천 종에게 서식지를 '제공한다'
det.analysis:
✅ ① muddy: 썰물 때 드러나는 '진흙투성이의' 환경이라는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② accumulated: 흙이 8,500년 넘게 바다로 흘러들어 '쌓였다'는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ blocks(막다) → provides(제공하다): 갯벌은 영양분이 풍부해 수천 종에게 서식지를 '제공한다'가 맞다. blocks는 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ④ globally: 22종의 '전 세계적으로' 멸종 위기이거나 그에 가까운 종을 포함한다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: provides(제공하다) ↔ blocks(막다). 서식지를 제공한다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① avoided → visited: 갯벌은 매년 약 118종의 철새가 '찾아온다'
det.analysis:
❌ ① avoided(피하다) → visited(찾아오다): 풍부한 생물 다양성 덕분에 갯벌은 약 118종의 철새가 '찾아온다'가 맞다. avoided는 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ② vital: 철새에게 갯벌은 '필수적인' 중간 기착지라는 문맥에 적절
✅ ③ rest: 갯벌이 없다면 긴 여정 동안 '쉴' 곳이 없다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ unique: 갯벌은 다양한 종으로 붐비는 '독특한' 생태계라는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: visited(찾아오다) ↔ avoided(피하다). 철새가 찾아온다

questions.passage: The Earth’s carbon can be divided into three ①<u>types</u>: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon.  Black carbon is ②<u>stored</u> while burning fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, and gas.  It causes the greenhouse effect, leading to global warming and climate change. It plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem because it absorbs carbon dioxide through ③<u>photosynthesis</u>.  Finally, blue carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine ecosystems such as ④<u>mangrove</u> wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② stored → released: 검은 탄소는 화석 연료를 태울 때 '방출된다'
det.analysis:
✅ ① types: 지구의 탄소는 세 가지 '유형'으로 나뉜다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② stored(저장된) → released(방출된): 검은 탄소는 석탄·석유·가스 같은 화석 연료를 '태울 때' 대기로 '방출되는(released)' 탄소이므로 released가 맞다. stored(저장)는 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ③ photosynthesis: 녹색 탄소는 '광합성'을 통해 이산화탄소를 흡수한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ mangrove: 파란 탄소가 저장되는 해양 생태계의 예로 '맹그로브' 습지가 나오는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: released(방출된) ↔ stored(저장된). 화석 연료를 태우면 탄소가 방출됨

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① toxins(독소): 서식지를 제공하는 풍요로운 갯벌과 어울리지 않음
❌ ② noise(소음): 흙 속 유기물과 관련이 없음
❌ ③ plastics(플라스틱): 자연 유기물에서 나오는 것이 아님
✅ ④ nutrients(영양분): 흙이 육지 동식물의 유기물을 포함하므로 갯벌은 '영양분'이 풍부하고 수천 종의 서식지를 제공한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
det.tip: organic matter(유기물) → rich in nutrients(영양분이 풍부)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① freeze(얼다): 물이 빠지지 않는 상황과 관련이 없음
❌ ② dry up(마르다): 물이 계속 차오르는 상황과 반대
✅ ③ overflow(넘치다): 물이 효과적으로 빠지지 않으면 욕조가 '넘친다'가 맞고, 이는 탄소 배출을 충분히 줄이지 않으면 대기 탄소가 계속 쌓인다는 비유와 이어짐 ← 정답
❌ ④ shrink(줄어들다): 물이 넘치는 상황과 반대
det.tip: if the water is not effectively drained(물이 빠지지 않으면) → overflow(넘친다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① carbon neutrality(탄소 중립): 배출된 탄소량과 흡수된 탄소량 사이의 '균형을 유지하는' 것을 뜻하므로, 이를 이루는 핵심 전략이 '탄소 중립'이라는 흐름에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ② global warming(지구 온난화): 해결해야 할 문제이지 달성할 전략이 아님
❌ ③ fossil fuel(화석 연료): 탄소를 배출하는 원인이라 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ greenhouse effect(온실 효과): 기후 변화의 원인이지 균형 전략이 아님
det.tip: a balance between carbon emitted and absorbed(배출·흡수 탄소의 균형) → carbon neutrality(탄소 중립)

❌ ③ melted: 녹았다 (관련 없음)

Blue Carbon and Getbol One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon in the atmosphere is to use the “good” carbon on Earth.  The Earth’s carbon can be divided into three types: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon.  Black carbon is released while burning fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, and gas.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 reduce와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① clean: 청소하다 (의미축이 다름)
❌ ② measure: 측정하다 (관련 없음)
❌ ③ store: 저장하다 (줄이는 것과 반대는 아님)
✅ ④ increase: 늘리다, 증가시키다 ← 정답
det.tip: reduce carbon emissions(탄소 배출을 줄이다) ↔ increase(늘리다)

questions.passage:
(A) The deep ocean can <u>store</u> huge amounts of carbon dioxide for thousands of years without releasing it back into the air.
(B) On his way home, he stopped by the <u>store</u> to buy some fresh bread and a bottle of milk.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 store의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) can store huge amounts of carbon dioxide는 바다가 많은 이산화탄소를 '저장하다'라는 동사이고, (B) stopped by the store to buy bread는 빵을 사러 들른 '가게'라는 명사 ← 정답
❌ ① (A)는 '가게'가 아니라 '저장하다'
❌ ③ (B)는 '보관하다'(동사)가 아니라 물건을 사는 '가게'(명사)
❌ ④ (A)는 '채우다'가 아니라 이산화탄소를 '저장하다'
det.tip: store: (A) 저장하다(동사) / (B) 가게(명사)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the natural environment in which a particular animal or plant normally lives"

det.analysis:
❌ ① glacier: 빙하 (오랜 세월 쌓인 얼음 덩어리)
❌ ② drought: 가뭄 (오랫동안 비가 오지 않는 상태)
✅ ③ habitat: 서식지 (특정 동식물이 보통 살아가는 자연 환경) ← 정답
❌ ④ emission: 배출 (기체 등을 내보내는 것)
det.tip: habitat = 특정 동식물이 살아가는 자연 서식지

questions.passage: To make matters worse, if the water is not effectively drained, the bathtub will overflow. In other words, if we don't reduce carbon emissions __________ (sufficient), atmospheric carbon will continue to accumulate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: sufficient(형용사, 충분한) → sufficiently(부사, 충분히): 빈칸은 동사 reduce(줄이다)를 꾸미는 자리이므로 부사가 와야 한다. '탄소 배출을 충분히 줄이지 않으면'이라는 뜻이 되도록 형용사 sufficient를 부사 sufficiently로 바꾼다.
det.tip: 동사(reduce)를 꾸미는 자리 → 부사 sufficiently

questions.passage: Considering that getbol contains numerous organisms and marine animals that store carbon, the treasure house of blue carbon has become a promising and __________ (sustain) solution to the current environmental problem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: sustain(동사, 유지하다) → sustainable(형용사, 지속 가능한): 빈칸은 뒤의 명사 solution(해결책)을 꾸미는 자리이고, 앞의 형용사 promising과 and로 나란히 이어진다. 따라서 동사 sustain을 형용사 sustainable로 바꿔 '지속 가능한 해결책'이라는 뜻이 되게 한다.
det.tip: 명사(solution)를 꾸미고 promising과 병렬 → 형용사 sustainable

questions.passage: Scientists worldwide are continuing to explore the capabilities of tidal flats with the goal of having them officially recognized as blue carbon.  Efforts to Protect Getbol Getbol in Korea was once considered useless muddy land, so much of it has been __________.  This has led to a decline in the area of tidal flats, causing a loss of biodiversity.  To prevent further damage to the marine ecosystem, both the government and environmental organizations have been making efforts to protect the tidal flats by regulating unnecessary development.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 reclaimed for farming and urbanization(농사와 도시화를 위해 매립되었다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① protected as a national park(국립공원으로 보호되었다): 뒤에 갯벌 면적이 '감소했다'는 부정적 결과가 이어지므로 반대
❌ ② turned into a wildlife reserve(야생 보호구역이 되었다): 생물 다양성 손실이라는 결과와 어긋남
❌ ③ left completely untouched(완전히 그대로 두었다): 면적이 줄었다는 문맥과 반대
✅ ④ reclaimed for farming and urbanization(농사와 도시화를 위해 매립되었다): 갯벌이 쓸모없는 땅으로 여겨져 많은 부분이 매립되었고, 그 결과 갯벌 면적이 줄어 생물 다양성이 손실되었다는 흐름에 맞음 ← 정답
det.tip: useless muddy land(쓸모없는 땅) + a decline in the area(면적 감소) → reclaimed for farming and urbanization

questions.passage: In fact, getbol is home to approximately 2,150 species of plants and animals, including 22 globally threatened or near-threatened species.  Thanks to its rich biodiversity, getbol is visited by about 118 species of migratory birds every year.  For millions of migratory birds that travel between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover location.  Without getbol, they would not have a place to rest and feed themselves during their long journeys, and they would __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① become extinct(멸종하다): 갯벌이 없으면 철새들이 긴 여정 동안 쉬고 먹을 곳이 없어 결국 '멸종할' 것이라는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ② travel much faster(훨씬 빨리 이동하다): 쉴 곳이 사라지는 상황과 관련이 없음
❌ ③ find new oceans(새로운 바다를 찾다): 본문에 근거가 없음
❌ ④ grow much larger(훨씬 커지다): 먹이·휴식처를 잃는 상황과 반대
det.tip: no place to rest and feed(쉬고 먹을 곳이 없음) → become extinct(멸종하다)
